content: This document provides important information about the medication containing elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir, commonly sold under the brand name Stribild. It is essential to understand that this information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the medication. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete guidance tailored to your health needs. Warning: If you have a hepatitis B infection, stopping this medication may worsen your symptoms or lead to severe complications. Do not discontinue the medication without consulting your doctor. Uses: This medication is used to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your overall quality of life. The medication contains four active components: Elvitegravir: An integrase inhibitor that prevents the virus from multiplying. Cobicistat: Enhances the effectiveness of elvitegravir. Emtricitabine and Tenofovir: Antiviral agents that help suppress the virus. It is important to note that this medication is not a cure for HIV. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, continue taking all prescribed HIV medications as directed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity and avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may come into contact with blood or bodily fluids. How to Use: Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully and take the medication exactly as prescribed. Take it at least two hours before or after using other products that may interfere with its effectiveness. For optimal results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not adjust your dosage or stop taking the medication without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time. Side Effects: Common side effects may include diarrhea, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, unusual dreams, back pain, or changes in skin color on your palms or soles. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In rare cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting treatment or months later. This medication may also cause severe, potentially fatal liver and blood problems, such as lactic acidosis. Tenofovir, one of the components, may increase the risk of bone loss. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, including the potential use of calcium and vitamin D supplements to mitigate bone loss. If you are at risk for bone loss, your doctor may monitor your bone mineral density. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. Precautions: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to any of its components (elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, or tenofovir) or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. The medication may cause dizziness, which can be worsened by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcohol consumption. This medication is not recommended during pregnancy, as it may not work effectively in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you are pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Emtricitabine and tenofovir can pass into breast milk, but it is unclear if elvitegravir or cobicistat do. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how this medication works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Do not take this medication with other HIV medications, such as ritonavir. This medication may slow the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications may impact how this drug is removed from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include mitotane, rifampin, and St. John’s wort. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (such as pills, patches, or rings), potentially leading to pregnancy. It may also increase the risk of side effects from hormonal birth control. Discuss alternative reliable birth control methods with your doctor and use effective barrier methods during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading HIV. Overdose: If someone overdoses and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: Attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in July 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and complete information about this medication.
